newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Ex-king can visit Romania "without difficulties".
newsitem.headline: Ex-king can visit Romania "without difficulties".

text.p: Romania's ex-king Michael, who was barred by the former leftist government from visiting his native land, will be allowed to enter Romania "without difficulties", the country's new foreign minister said on Tuesday.
"From a political point of view, we see no difficulty for the former sovereign of Romania to visit the country," Adrian Severin told a news conference.
Severin's remarks were in response to a Christmas address sent by Michael to Romanians from his exile in Switzerland.
"I know that I will be soon with you, after a long and unjust separation," Michael's statement said.

"We will see to which extent the foreign ministry is involved in this problem and we will act accordingly," Severin said in a first official reference to the thorny monarchy issue since the new centrist government took office this month.

The defeated leftist cabinet, apparently fearing his enormous popularity, had refused to let Michael in since an emotional Orthodox Easter visit in 1992 when he drew hundreds of thousands of well-wishers.
Michael was deposed from the throne by Moscow-backed communists who seized power in Romania after World War Two, and was forced into exile in 1947.
His last attempt to return home a year ago was thwarted when authorities bundled him back on to a plane at Bucharest airport.

Both ex-president Ion Iliescu, a former top communist, and his leftist Party of Social Democracy had used the ex-king in their campaign to scare voters away from the centrist political forces saying they wanted to restore the monarchy.
Michael still wields influence in Romania though he was written out of the 1991 post-communist constitution which defines the country as a presidential republic.
